files.README.md:
# MindContext Core

MindContext Core is session persistence infrastructure for coding agents, built on composable hooks that keep you in context across sessions.

## How it works

Every time you start a Claude Code session, Claude has no idea what you were working on yesterday. Memory compaction wipes out your decisions. Context switching means re-explaining everything.

MindContext Core fixes this.

When your session starts, hooks automatically inject your current work context—the issue you're implementing, where you left off, which files are hot. You don't have to remember or re-explain anything.

When you're ready to work, you type `/next`. It finds your in-progress issue, or recommends ready tasks ranked by impact score. No hunting through task lists or trying to remember what was blocked.

When you want to save progress notes, `/comment` saves a context summary to the current task—either your own text or an auto-generated summary from conversation context. Your notes become comments on beads issues, not ephemeral session state that disappears.

When you come back tomorrow, it all gets re-injected automatically. You pick up exactly where you left off.

The system is designed to be minimal and compatible. It doesn't enforce a methodology—it provides the foundation that any workflow can build on. Use it with OpenSpec for spec-driven development, with superpowers for TDD enforcement, or on its own for just session persistence.


## Installation

```bash
# Add marketplace
/plugin marketplace add tmsjngx0/mindcontext-core

# Install
/plugin install mindcontext-core@tmsjngx0
```

Verify with `/help`—you should see `/next`, `/comment`, `/commit`, `/project-init`.


## The Basic Workflow

1. **SessionStart** - Activates when session begins. Injects your in-progress beads issue, HOT files to read, progress notes from last session. You start with context, not a blank slate.

2. **`/next`** - Activates when you need work. Shows in-progress issues or recommends ready tasks ranked by impact score (unblock count, priority, epic continuity).

3. **Implementation** - You write code. Hooks stay out of the way. PreToolUse validates CHANGELOG/README updates before commits. Stop hook updates timestamps.

4. **`/comment`** - Save progress notes anytime. Auto-generates a session summary from conversation context, or accepts free text. Notes persist as beads comments.

6. **SessionEnd** - Activates when session ends. Syncs beads to git remote, cleans up. Your state is persisted, ready for next time.

**The hooks run automatically.** Session persistence without friction.


## What's Inside

### Hooks (7 Lifecycle Events)

| Hook | When | What |
|------|------|------|
| **SessionStart** | Session begins | Inject beads context, P0 continuations, HOT files, detect installed plugins |
| **UserPromptSubmit** | Before processing | Workflow reminders, TDD mode if active |
| **PreToolUse** | Before Bash (git) | CHANGELOG/README validation |
| **PreToolUse** | Before `br create` | Bead quality enforcement (self-containment check) |
| **Stop** | Between responses | Update last_active timestamp |
| **PreCompact** | Before compaction | Preserve critical context |
| **SessionEnd** | Session ends | Sync beads, cleanup |

### Skills

| Skill | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| **`/next`** | Work discovery. Find in-progress work or recommend ready tasks ranked by impact score (unblock count × 3 + priority + epic bonus). |
| **`/comment`** | Session notes. Save progress to current in-progress task — auto-summary via note-generator agent or free text. |
| **`/bd-sync`** | OpenSpec ↔ beads synchronization. Thin router delegating to 5 specialized agents: `audit`, `import` (beads-builder), `import --lite` (sync-importer), `update`, `specgap`. Supports `--skip-tdd`, `--containment`, `--max-bead-size`, `--quality` flags. |
| **`/commit`** | Conventional Commits. Syncs with remote (stash/pull --rebase/pop) before delegating analysis to commit-worker agent. Auto-resolves additive merge conflicts. |
| **`/impl`** | Autonomous beads task implementation. Spawns impl-worker (Sonnet), commit-worker (Haiku), verify-worker (Haiku) in background pipeline. Sequential (default) or `--swarm` parallel mode. Filter with `--label` or `--epic`. |
| **`/plan-decompose`** | Decompose plans into beads epics. Skeleton-first: ALL tasks get lightweight descriptions by default. Use `/enrich` to promote tasks when ready to implement. Use `--enrich-all` for legacy self-contained mode with TDD chain (`TEST → IMPL → TIDY`). Flags: `--with-features`, `--with-release`, `--with-pr`, `--dry-run`. |
| **`/enrich`** | Promote lightweight `iteration:future` beads to self-contained descriptions with TDD chain (test + impl + tidy beads). Single bead or `--epic --ready` batch mode. |
| **`/tdd`** | TDD workflow reference. Separate RED/GREEN/REFACTOR commits that prove the methodology was followed. |

### Agents (12 Specialized Workers)

Commands and skills delegate formulaic work to specialized agents, reducing token consumption by 60-80%.

| Agent | Model | Purpose |
|-------|-------|---------|
| `impl-worker` | sonnet | Implement code from self-contained beads task descriptions, return structured JSON |
| `verify-worker` | haiku | Post-commit validation: type-checking, linting, targeted test execution |
| `commit-worker` | haiku | Analyze git changes, produce granular conventional commit groups as JSON |
| `sync-auditor` | haiku | Cross-reference OpenSpec changes against beads epics, find gaps and drift with quality grading |
| `sync-importer` | sonnet | Parse OpenSpec proposals, create lightweight tracking beads (`--lite` mode) |
| `plan-decomposer` | opus | Decompose plans into beads epic + lightweight skeleton subtasks + blocking deps. Use /enrich to promote. |
| `beads-builder` | opus | Create implementation-ready, self-contained beads with TDD test-bead-first (default import) |
| `bead-enricher` | sonnet | Enrich existing bead descriptions for self-containment and implementation readiness |
| `sync-updater` | haiku | Compare tasks.md against beads children, synchronize bidirectionally |
| `specgap-scanner` | haiku | Find untracked commits, TODO/FIXME comments, new files without beads tasks |
| `file-classifier` | haiku | Classify session files into HOT/WARM/COLD tiers for context continuation |
| `note-generator` | haiku | Generate session progress notes for `/comment` |

**Pattern:** Command = orchestrator (user interaction), Agent = executor (structured output, no user interaction).

### Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `/project-init` | Initialize project with CLAUDE.md, beads, workflow selection |
| `/changelog` | Update CHANGELOG.md following Keep a Changelog |
| `/audit-claude-md` | Restructure CLAUDE.md for clarity |


## Migrating from v2.x

If you used the old commands, here's what changed:

| Old Command | New Equivalent |
|-------------|----------------|
| `/prime-context` | `/next` (auto-shows status on first run) |
| `/update-context` | `/comment` (saves notes to beads) |
| `/focus` | `br list --status=in_progress` |
| `focus.json` | Beads comments (via `/comment`) |
| `/next shift` | `/comment` + `/next` |
| `/next complete` | `br close <id>` |
| `/next continue` | `/comment` |

The old commands were removed in v0.3.8. Use `/next` to find work, `/comment` to save notes.


## Session Notes

`/comment` saves structured progress notes to beads issues. Notes persist across memory compaction and session boundaries, providing context recovery without re-explanation.


## Integration Detection

Core auto-detects installed plugins and adapts:

| Plugin | Detection | Behavior |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| beads | `.beads/` directory | Show in-progress issues, sync on session end |
| OpenSpec | `openspec/` directory | Available for spec-driven workflows |
| feature-dev | `installed_plugins.json` | Inject TDD enforcement context |
| superpowers | `installed_plugins.json` | Compatible, no conflicts |


## Philosophy

- **Minimal** - Just session management, no opinions on methodology
- **Compatible** - Works with any workflow plugin without conflicts
- **Persistent** - Uses beads comments for state that survives memory compaction
- **Efficient** - File tiers and self-contained descriptions save tokens
- **Foundation** - The layer that everything else builds on


## Roadmap

MindContext is evolving toward a **CLI-first, agent-agnostic platform**. The future isn't "a Claude Code plugin"—it's an orchestration layer that works with any coding agent.

### Now (v0.5.0)
- **Iteration-based workflow** - Dual-track (Discovery + Delivery), size routing (XS/S/M/L), spike guidelines, reflect phase
- **Lightweight-first decomposition** - Future tasks stay minimal; current iteration gets self-contained descriptions
- **`/enrich`** - Promote lightweight beads to implementation-ready when their iteration starts
- **Agent delegation** - 12 specialized agents reduce token consumption by 60-80%
- Thin orchestrator pattern: commands route, agents execute
- Session hooks with memory compaction preservation
- TDD enforcement with separate RED/GREEN/REFACTOR commits

### Soon (Q2 2026)
- **CLI-first architecture** - `mctx` CLI that bridges openspec ↔ beads ↔ feature-dev
- **Agent portability** - Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Aider, any CLI tool
- **Implementation planning** - Full planning workflow with detailed guides for hand-coding
- **Parent-submodule awareness** - Unified context across monorepos and worktrees

### Later (Q3 2026)
- **MCP bridges** - Multi-LLM routing via standardized adapters
- **Release automation** - Streamlined version bumping for plugin workflows

Track progress at [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/tmsjngx0/mindcontext-core/issues).


## Works With

MindContext Core is designed as the foundation layer. Combine with:

| Plugin | What it adds |
|--------|--------------|
| **beads** | Git-backed issue tracking with dependencies |
| **OpenSpec** | Spec-driven development with change proposals |
| **superpowers** | TDD enforcement, micro-task planning |
| **feature-dev** | Codebase exploration, architecture guidance |

**Recommended stack:** Core + beads + OpenSpec + feature-dev


## Contributing

Changes go through OpenSpec proposals:

1. Fork the repository
2. Create `openspec/changes/your-feature/` with spec files
3. Follow the [OpenSpec workflow](https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec)
4. Submit a PR

See `openspec/AGENTS.md` for the complete guide.


## Updating

```bash
/plugin update mindcontext-core
```
